items.stem: How does a typical GraphQL API differ from a typical REST API in how clients fetch data?

options.text: Clients query a single endpoint and ask for exactly the fields they need
options.rationale: Correct: GraphQL exposes one endpoint and lets clients shape the response.

options.text: Each resource must have its own URL and fixed response shape
options.rationale: That is the REST style GraphQL is being contrasted with.

options.text: GraphQL cannot express relationships between types
options.rationale: GraphQL is built around typed relationships between objects.

options.text: GraphQL responses are always larger than REST responses
options.rationale: GraphQL often reduces over-fetching by returning only requested fields.

items.explanation: Correct: GraphQL exposes one endpoint and lets clients shape the response.

items.stem: Select TWO effective ways to address the N+1 query problem in a GraphQL resolver layer.

options.text: Batch related lookups within a tick using a dataloader
options.rationale: Correct: dataloaders batch many lookups into fewer queries.

options.text: Cache repeated lookups for the duration of a request
options.rationale: Correct: per-request caching avoids repeating identical lookups.

options.text: Issue one database query per item in a list
options.rationale: That is exactly the N+1 pattern being avoided.

options.text: Remove all relationships from the schema
options.rationale: Stripping relationships breaks the API rather than fixing performance.

options.text: Disable the resolver and return null
options.rationale: Returning null removes functionality, not the performance root cause.

items.explanation: Correct: dataloaders batch many lookups into fewer queries.

items.stem: Why add query depth or complexity limits to a public GraphQL API?

options.text: To prevent abusive, arbitrarily deep or expensive queries from overloading the server
options.rationale: Correct: cost/depth limits protect the server from expensive or malicious queries.

options.text: To force every client to use REST instead
options.rationale: Limits constrain queries; they do not switch the protocol.
Limits do not change the type system.

options.text: To remove the need for authentication
options.rationale: Query limits do not replace authentication or authorization.

items.explanation: Correct: cost/depth limits protect the server from expensive or malicious queries.
